references.text: Abel also brings an offering to God, but from the firstborn of his flock and their fat. The contrast between the two offerings is central to the subsequent narrative.
The law concerning the grain offering (mincha) – the same Hebrew word used for Cain's offering in Gen 4:3. This shows that offerings of the earth's produce had a place in Israel's worship.
By faith Abel offered a better sacrifice than Cain. The book of Hebrews interprets the difference between the two offerings as a matter of faith.
The call to honor the Lord with one's wealth and the firstfruits of all one's harvest is thematically linked to Cain's offering of the earth's produce.
The best of the oil, the new wine, and the grain – the firstfruits given to the Lord – illustrate the principle of giving the best to God, which sheds light on Cain's offering.
